cards.explanation: The answer is earth. The call goes out wide: "Hear, O peoples, all of you; listen, O earth, and everyone in it!" (Micah 1:2). That's every people and everybody on the earth, with nobody left standing in the back. When a message starts like that, friends, you put down your spatula and listen.

The answer is that the mountains will melt like wax. The text says, "The mountains will melt beneath Him… like wax before the fire" (Micah 1:4). Friends, I've watched a cookie box get left by the oven, and a mountain doing that is a whole different thing. The picture shows how great the LORD is when He comes down.

The answer is that the valleys will split apart. The text says, "…the valleys will split apart…" (Micah 1:4). So the mountains melt on top and the valleys crack open down below. Picture a cookie that cracks straight down the middle when it comes out of the oven, friends, only this is a whole valley.

The answer is the sins of Israel. "All this is for the transgression of Jacob and the sins of the house of Israel." (Micah 1:5). The melting and splitting aren't random, friends. The text ties them straight to those sins. Then it asks what the transgression of Jacob is, and answers with Samaria.

The answer is a planting area for a vineyard. The message says Samaria will be "…a heap of rubble in the open field, a planting area for a vineyard." (Micah 1:6). Think about that, friends. A whole city, and the spot ends up as a place to plant vines.

The answer is idols. Verse 7 says, "…I will destroy all her idols." It also says that all her carved images will be smashed to pieces (Micah 1:7). So, friends, the idols are on the list of what goes down along with the city.

The answer is True. Right after the word against Samaria comes "Because of this I will lament and wail…" (Micah 1:8). The words come in a first-person voice, and the text doesn't say whose voice it is, so I'll leave that open. What I can tell you, friends, is that grief comes right on the heels of the judgment.

The answer is False. Micah 1:9 says the wound "…has reached even Judah; it has approached the gate of my people, as far as Jerusalem itself." It doesn't stop at Samaria, friends. It keeps on going until it's at Jerusalem's door.

The answer is in mourning for their children. The text says, "Shave yourselves bald and cut off your hair in mourning for your precious children…" (Micah 1:16). Children are called precious right there in the verse, friends. That tells you this mourning is a deep one.
The answer is exile. The children "…will go from you into exile." (Micah 1:16). That's the reason for the mourning, friends, and it's a heavy one. I think this is one of those lines you read slowly.
